    {"name": "helpfulness_ratio", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "A genuine new axis derived from HelpfulnessNumerator/Denominator; distinct signal for modeling score."},
    {"name": "summary_length", "analytical_usefulness": 0.4, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Length of Summary; generic surface feature with limited leverage but soundly derived."},

    {"name": "question_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.5, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Mostly zero (near-constant) but captures a weak stylistic signal; grounded in Text."},
    {"name": "uppercase_ratio", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Emphasis/shouting proxy that can relate to sentiment; correctly computed from Text characters."},
    {"name": "positive_keyword_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Sentiment lexicon count is directly relevant to predicting score; values are lexicon-dependent so 'great/yummy=2' is sound while some positive rows scored 0, but this is defensible given a fixed keyword list."},
    {"name": "negative_keyword_count", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.9, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Negative sentiment count gives useful signal for score prediction; grounded in Text via a keyword list."},
    {"name": "review_year", "analytical_usefulness": 0.6, "source_groundedness": 1.0, "hallucination_observed": false, "rationale": "Temporal feature extracted from Time; provides a grouping/trend axis and years are plausibly derived from timestamps."}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.6,
  "source_groundedness": 0.97,
  "rationale": "The added columns are all soundly derived from present fields (Text, Summary, Helpfulness*, Time) with no observed hallucinations; a 'silent' row correctly yields 0 counts.
